name: Buns, Booze & Bucks Simulator
detailed_description:
Welcome to 1920s London, where foggy streets hide secrets, and every other person is either a gangster or an informant. In Mafia Bakery, you’ll take on the role of a young criminal who, under the guise of baking bread, runs a bootleg alcohol operation. Sounds simple enough: just bake and brew, right? But remember: one wrong move, and your business will collapse faster than you can say, "Hey, it’s just buns!" 

Parallel management of two businesses

For the people of London, you are the owner of a small bakery, where you need to serve customers, monitor the quality of bread products and maintain a reputation. For those who know the truth, you are a moonshiner who creates unique drinks for smuggling. One process should not interfere with the other, otherwise serious consequences await you. For example, if the dough dries out, housewives will start complaining, and if the alcohol ferments, the whole batch will be ruined, and you will owe a lot of money to the bad guys.

Creating Alcohol

From braga to distillation, every stage of production requires attention. Experiment with ingredients (from fruits to... mushrooms?) to create drinks with different flavors and effects. Be careful: mistakes can lead to explosions or damage to the batch. Add too much chili and you'll find out how hot your customers are.

Customer service

Different types of customers come to your bakery: housewives, workers, inspectors, and even competitors. Each of them has its own preferences and requirements. One mistake, and the police might come to check. And if you sell stale bread to a drunk, he can start a fight right in the hall.

Smuggling and strategy

Your task is to deliver alcohol to the pier, bypassing customs officers, competitors and "rats". Choose reliable routes, negotiate with gangs, and pay bribes to protect your business. Give it to the informant's paw so that your paws are not handcuffed.

Development and modernization

Upgrade your equipment, expand your product range, and discover new recipes. The better your product, the more money you will earn. But don't forget: the bigger the business, the more attention it attracts. The police may suspect that the baker can hardly afford a Rolls-Royce, but if this is the legacy of a deceased uncle, then it's a completely different matter.
